Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: measurement & crediting details

Jane — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a concise proposal (PDF) and a CSV with sample monthly calculations. High level summary up front:

- Measurement vantage: Redwood computes per-tenant availability from the control-plane metrics and per-region serving telemetry. We use identical windowing for availability and latency (1-minute buckets, sampled at request completion).
- Aggregation & SLOs: primary latency SLO is p95 of request-complete latency at 1-minute resolution; availability is percent of 1-minute buckets with successful 200-level responses above a minimum throughput threshold.
- Partial outages: we partition availability by region + routing tier and attribute credits only to the affected routing scope (tenant-region). Global fallbacks are documented; credits apply if the root cause is Redwood-controlled capacity or software regressions.

Worked example (monthly):
- Customer monthly bill: $120,000
- Observed monthly availability (tenant-us-west): 99.80%
- Committed availability in contract: 99.95%
- Delta: 0.15% below target
- Redwood credit policy: credit = min(30%, ((target - observed) / (1 - target)) * 100)% applied to monthly bill (example formula shown in appendix).
- Example credit: ((0.9995 - 0.9980) / (1 - 0.9995)) = 0.0015 / 0.0005 = 3 => capped at 30% => 30% credit => $36,000

We attach: Redwood_Instrumentation_Crediting_Proposal_v1.1.pdf (non-technical explainer + methodology appendix) and SLA-sample-report-20270320.csv (sample telemetry export and worked calculations).

Quick ask: can you confirm whether Acme wants p95 or p99 latency reported in the SLO? We can provide both, but billing-credit triggers are typically tied to availability only.

Thanks,

Subject: internal: small edits to calculation language before sending

Soojin — quick internal note before we finalize the external reply. A few suggestions to make the credit calc defensible to procurement/legal:

- Spell out that sampling granularity is 1-minute NTP-synced buckets; include clock-skew tolerance (<=250ms) and how we handle late-arriving telemetry (we backfill up to 10s).
- Replace the shorthand credit formula with a step-by-step worked table (percent gap -> multiplier -> capped credit) — procurement likes a deterministic table.
- Clarify failure attribution: credits only apply when root cause is Redwood (software / serving infra) and not client or third-party network. Provide example scenarios for each attribution case.

I drafted a 3-row worked table you can paste into the appendix. Also suggest we offer a short one-hour technical review call with Acme's SREs to walk through telemetry signals and sampling.

Happy to jump on the call; let me know available times.

—Lauren (on behalf of Solutions Ops)

Subject: Re: Instrumentation & Crediting Workflow Proposal for RFP #ACME-2027

Jane — following up with the revised appendix per Lauren's notes and a suggested next step. Key clarifications added to the attached PDF and sample CSV:

- Bucketing & clocking: 1-minute NTP-synced buckets at the ingestion point; clock skew tolerance 250ms; late telemetry backfill window = 10s (backfilled into the originating 1-minute bucket).
- Latency SLO reporting: we will publish both p95 and p99. Credit eligibility is tied to availability only (per contract) but we can include latency regressions in a monthly health report.
- Attribution policy: credits apply only when Redwood determines the root cause = Redwood-controlled software or serving capacity. Outages caused by customer-configured rate limits, client network outages, or upstream third-party connectors are excluded. We will provide incident RCA artifacts on request.

Worked credit table (appendix):
- Target 99.95% (monthly) | Observed 99.80% | Gap 0.15% | Raw multiplier = 3.0x | Credit before cap = 300% -> capped at 30% -> Credit = 30% of monthly invoice
- Target 99.95% | Observed 99.90% | Gap 0.05% | Raw multiplier = 1.0x | Credit = 10% of monthly invoice
- Target 99.99% | Observed 99.98% | Gap 0.01% | Raw multiplier = 0.2x | Credit = 2% of monthly invoice

Next steps:
1) We can do a 1-hour technical walkthrough with your SREs to validate telemetry and export format (we've proposed Wed 3/31 10:00-11:00 PT). Please confirm availability.
2) If agreed, Redwood will include the revised appendix and the worked CSV in the final legal submission.
